Package de.nexus.antixray.api

Schnittstelle NexusAntiXRayApi

public interface NexusAntiXRayApi
Entry point of the NexusAntiXRay API.

Getting the instance


 NexusAntiXRayApi api = NexusAntiXRayApi.get();
get() throws an IllegalStateException with an explanation while NexusAntiXRay is not enabled. The same instance is registered with Bukkit's ServicesManager, so Bukkit.getServicesManager().load(NexusAntiXRayApi.class) returns it too, or null instead of throwing.

Before the first use of any class of this API, check Bukkit.getPluginManager().isPluginEnabled("NexusAntiXRay"), even if your plugin declares depend: [NexusAntiXRay]. The API classes live in the NexusAntiXRay jar. If the plugin is missing, or if it disabled itself while starting (for example because no license key is set), the classes cannot be loaded at all and the first line of your code that touches one fails with a NoClassDefFoundError, before get() can explain anything. Bukkit enables a depending plugin in both cases.

NexusAntiXRay registers the API at the end of its onEnable and removes it first thing in onDisable. An instance that is kept after that point stays safe to call, but answers like a server without players: the queries return false or null (loadStats(java.util.UUID) a future that is completed with null) and the actions do nothing. Do not keep the instance across a disable; calling get() again is cheap.

Threads

Every method of this interface may be called from any thread: the server thread, a Folia region or entity thread, the global region thread or an asynchronous task. The methods only read and change NexusAntiXRay's own state, which is built for concurrent access; none of them touches the world. What a query returns is a snapshot: hidden blocks are revealed and hidden again all the time by the ray tracing threads.

loadStats(java.util.UUID) is the one method that reads from disk. It does so on a thread of NexusAntiXRay and hands the result to a CompletableFuture; the thread your callback runs on is not specified, see there.

The events in de.nexus.antixray.api.event are different: each of them is fired on one specific thread, which its class documentation names.

Errors

A null argument is the caller's mistake and is answered with an IllegalArgumentException. Apart from that no method throws. Players that are offline or not known to NexusAntiXRay yet, disabled worlds and a disabled plugin all lead to the neutral results described at each method. Should NexusAntiXRay fail internally, it logs the problem once and returns the same neutral result.

Compatibility

The API follows semantic versioning on its own, independent of the plugin version (see API_VERSION). Within a major version nothing is removed or changed, only added. This interface is implemented by NexusAntiXRay alone: new methods in a minor version are not a breaking change, so do not implement it in your plugin.
Seit:
1.0.0

      It is a compile-time constant, so the Java compiler copies its value into your plugin. Read from your code it is the version you compiled against. The version that is running on the server comes from apiVersion().

  • Methodendetails

    • get

      static NexusAntiXRayApi get()
      Returns the API of the running NexusAntiXRay plugin.

      The instance is looked up in Bukkit's ServicesManager. May be called from any thread.

      The API classes must come from the NexusAntiXRay plugin at runtime. If a plugin shades its own copy of the API jar, that copy is a different set of classes: this method does not find the plugin and event listeners registered through the copy are never called. The copy can also be handed to other plugins on the same server, which then fail the same way; the message of the exception names the plugin the classes were loaded from. Depend on the jar with compileOnly (Gradle) or scope provided (Maven).

      This method can only explain a problem while the API classes can be loaded. That is the case if it is called too early (before NexusAntiXRay was enabled), after NexusAntiXRay was disabled while the server is running, or through a shaded copy. If NexusAntiXRay is not installed or disabled itself during startup, the classes are not there and the caller gets a NoClassDefFoundError instead; see the class description for the check that avoids it.

      Gibt zurück:
      the API, never null
      Löst aus:
      IllegalStateException - if NexusAntiXRay is not enabled (yet, or any more), or if the API classes in use are a copy that does not belong to the running plugin. The message says which.
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • apiVersion

      String apiVersion()
      The API version the running plugin implements, as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

      Use it before calling a method that is newer than 1.0.0: on a server with an older NexusAntiXRay that method does not exist and the call would fail with a NoSuchMethodError. isApiAtLeast(int, int) does the comparison for you.

      Thread: any.

      Gibt zurück:
      the running API version, for example "1.0.0"

      default boolean isApiAtLeast(int major, int minor)
      Tells whether the running API is at least the given version of the same major line.

    • isBypassed

      boolean isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Tells whether the anti-xray filter is currently switched off for a player.

      A bypassed player gets the world unmodified (nothing hidden, no fake ores, no culling) and is left out of the x-ray detection. The state comes from two sources:

      • the permission nexusantixray-autobypass, read when the player joins and then about every two seconds, and
      • the session switch set by /nax bypass or setBypass(org.bukkit.entity.Player, boolean). While it is set it wins over the permission, in both directions.
      The session switch is dropped when the player leaves and whenever the permission changes (granted or revoked); from then on the permission decides again.

      Offline players, and players whose join NexusAntiXRay has not seen yet, are not bypassed: the result is false. A session starts with NexusAntiXRay's own handler of the PlayerJoinEvent (priority LOW), which reads the permission; from there on the result is reliable. It ends with the connection: inside a PlayerQuitEvent the result may already be false for a player who was bypassed a moment ago. A plugin that needs the last state of a leaving player keeps track of it with the BypassChangeEvent.

      The state belongs to the player, not to a world, so it is also reported in a world listed under worlds.disabled (where nothing is hidden anyway).

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      player - the player, not null
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the filter is off for this player
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if player is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0
      Siehe auch:
      • BypassChangeEvent

    • setBypass

      boolean setBypass(org.bukkit.entity.Player player, boolean bypass)
      Sets the session switch of a player, exactly like /nax bypass does (which toggles it).

      true switches the filter off for this player, false switches it on, also for a player who has the permission nexusantixray-autobypass. The switch holds until the player leaves, until it is set again, or until the permission of the player changes; see isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player). There is no persistent state: after a rejoin the permission decides.

      If the call changes the effective state, the player's chunks are sent again (hidden again or unmodified) and a BypassChangeEvent with cause API follows on the thread of the player. If the player already is in the requested state, only the switch is set and no event is fired.

      The method works from the PlayerJoinEvent on, for every handler that runs after NexusAntiXRay's own (priority LOW; a plugin that depends on NexusAntiXRay and listens with LOW or later is on the safe side). A switch set there is in place before the player receives the first chunk. For offline players and during the login events nothing happens and the result is false. Do not call the method from a join handler with priority LOWEST: NexusAntiXRay has not read the permission yet, so the call usually returns false, and a switch it does set is dropped again if the player has the permission. A player who is leaving is no better: inside a PlayerQuitEvent the call may or may not still reach the player, and the switch ends with the session anyway.

      In a world listed under worlds.disabled the state is stored and applies as soon as the player enters another world.

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      player - the player, not null
      bypass - true to switch the filter off for the player, false to switch it on
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the player is tracked and now has the requested state, whether or not the call changed anything; false if the player is not tracked and nothing was done. To learn whether the state changed, compare isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player) before the call or listen to the event.
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if player is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • isFeatureActive

      boolean isFeatureActive(AntiXRayFeature feature, org.bukkit.World world)
      Tells whether a feature is switched on in a world.

      This is the effective switch after the world rules of config.yml: a world listed under worlds.disabled has every feature off, otherwise worlds.overrides.<world>.features wins over the global features section. Reloads and /nax feature take effect immediately.

      The answer is about the world, not about a player. For one player the feature is at work if this method returns true and isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player) returns false.

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      feature - the feature, not null
      world - the world, not null
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the feature is on in this world
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an argument is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • isHidden

      boolean isHidden(org.bukkit.entity.Player player, org.bukkit.block.Block block)
      Tells whether the client of a player currently shows a replacement instead of this block.

      true means NexusAntiXRay has sent the player something else for this position and has not revealed the real block since. That covers

      • blocks of the hide list (AntiXRayFeature.HIDE_BLOCKS) that the player has no line of sight to,
      • hidden block entities such as chests (AntiXRayFeature.TILE_CULLING), and
      • every position inside a structure that is still filled for the player (AntiXRayFeature.STRUCTURE_CULLING), air included.
      A fake ore is not a hidden block: at such a position the server has ordinary stone and the client shows an ore that does not exist. This method returns false there. Entities and masked light are not blocks and are not covered either.

      The result is false whenever nothing is replaced for the player at this position: the block is of a type that is not hidden, it has been revealed, the player is bypassed, the feature or the whole world is disabled, the block is in another world than the player, its chunk has not been sent to the player (also before the first chunk after a join), or the player is offline.

      The bypass counts from the moment it changes: as soon as isBypassed(org.bukkit.entity.Player) returns true this method returns false for every block, and after the bypass ended hidden blocks are reported as hidden again. The client catches up within the following ticks, while the chunks are sent again.

      The answer is a snapshot. The ray tracing threads reveal a block within a few ticks after the player gets a line of sight and may hide it again later (blocks.rehide).

      Thread: any. Only the coordinates and the world of block are read, never its type.

      Parameter:
      player - the player whose view is asked for, not null
      block - the block, not null
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the player currently gets a replacement for this block
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an argument is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • refresh

      boolean refresh(org.bukkit.entity.Player player)
      Hides everything again for a player and sends the player's chunks again, like /nax refresh <player>.

      Blocks, block entities and structures the player has already uncovered are hidden again; the next ray tracing pass, a few ticks later, reveals what the player can see. The chunks are sent again over the following ticks, the nearest first. Use it after your plugin changed something NexusAntiXRay cannot notice by itself. It is not needed after setBypass(org.bukkit.entity.Player, boolean).

      For a bypassed player and in a world listed under worlds.disabled there is nothing to hide; the call has no visible effect there. Nothing happens for a player NexusAntiXRay does not track (offline, or the join packet has not been sent yet).

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      player - the player, not null
      Gibt zurück:
      true if the player is tracked and the refresh was queued, false otherwise
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if player is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • getStats

      MiningStats getStats(UUID playerId)
      Returns the mining statistics NexusAntiXRay holds in memory for a player.

      Statistics exist from the first block a player breaks while being counted by the x-ray detection (survival or adventure mode, fake ores active for the player, xray-detection.enabled). They are kept after the player leaves, until the server stops or until the entry makes room for more recently active players. This method never reads from disk and never blocks: it reports the detection window and the totals of the current server run only. The totals across restarts come from loadStats(java.util.UUID).

      While a player is bypassed or in a world listed under worlds.disabled, nothing is counted; statistics collected before stay available.

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      playerId - the unique id of the player (online or offline), not null
      Gibt zurück:
      an immutable snapshot, or null if there are no statistics in memory for this player
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if playerId is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0
      Siehe auch:
      • loadStats(java.util.UUID)

    • loadStats

      CompletableFuture<StoredMiningStats> loadStats(UUID playerId)
      Loads the totals NexusAntiXRay has stored for a player across server restarts.

      NexusAntiXRay keeps the totals of every counted player, online or offline, in its statistics storage (a file in the plugin folder, see xray-detection.storage in config.yml). This method reads them from there. The read happens on a thread of NexusAntiXRay; the calling thread is never blocked, and the result arrives through the returned future. It includes what has been counted but not written yet.

      The future completes with null when there is nothing to hand out:

      • nothing is stored for this player (never counted, or the record was removed after xray-detection.storage.retention-days days without a visit),
      • the storage is switched off (xray-detection.storage.enabled) or could not be opened,
      • NexusAntiXRay is disabled, or is disabled while the request is waiting,
      • reading failed (NexusAntiXRay logs the reason), or
      • too many requests are waiting already.
      The future never completes exceptionally, and the method never returns null. Every call returns a future of its own; completing or cancelling it yourself affects nobody else.

      Do not poll. Every call is a read from disk, and all of them share one thread with the writes of the detection. For numbers that change while a player is mining use getStats(java.util.UUID), which answers from memory. Load the stored totals when you need them: for a command, when a player joins, for a report.

      The callback thread is not specified. Functions attached to the future (thenAccept, thenApply, ...) usually run on an asynchronous thread, but they run on the calling thread if the result is already there when they are attached (storage off, plugin disabled), and on the thread that disables NexusAntiXRay for requests that were still waiting then. Switch to your own scheduler before you touch the Bukkit API.

      Never wait for the result on a server thread. join() or get() on the main thread, a Folia region thread or inside an event handler stalls the server for as long as the disk takes, and for several seconds if another program holds the database file.

      Thread: any.

      Parameter:
      playerId - the unique id of the player (online or offline), not null
      Gibt zurück:
      a future that completes with an immutable snapshot of the stored totals, or with null in the cases listed above; never null itself
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if playerId is null
      Seit:
      1.0.0
      Siehe auch:
      • getStats(java.util.UUID)
